director_mandate.binding_question_summary: Convert the parent non-result (every admitted item at max hop <= 1) into a hop-depth re-acquisition cost-scaling law on the credential-free GET-only stdlib-HTTP substrate, with a falsifier arithmetically checkable before freeze and satisfiable in BOTH directions.
four_binding_preconditions: pre-freeze control certificate: all four controls live-verified PASS with evidence refs inside spec.json BEFORE freeze.json (repairs parent VN-02)
baseline-ordering argument, proven before freeze, that the re-derivation comparator is strictly more expensive than re-acquisition by construction, so the break-even accept region is non-empty
paired per-item medians over the SAME item set plus a materiality guard on the break-even denominator
drop the five-class stationarity taxonomy entirely or make every declared class reachable by evaluation order

question: On the credential-free GET-only stdlib-HTTP substrate, over a frozen target pool large enough to admit state-carrying items at shortest-path hop >= 3, how does the unconditional cost of obtaining ONE fresh valid instance of a state item scale with the item's shortest-path hop distance from the host root, measured in GET requests (primary channel; stdlib-only) and response-body bytes (size channel; cl100k_base tokens recorded only if a tokenizer is importable and its version is recorded), and is that cost flat or growing? The experiment replaces the parent's undecidable stationarity LABEL with a cost SCALING LAW on the same free substrate, because the parent measured only hop 0..1 where one or two unconditional GETs already reach the item.

operational_definitions.substrate: HTTP GET only via Python stdlib urllib; TLS verified; frozen User-Agent 'SPIDER-research-frontier-37950626378/1.0'; timeout 12s; max response body 600000 bytes; redirects followed; no credentials, cookies, browser, Docker, model key or write verb.
operational_definitions.navigation_graph: Directed graph whose nodes are defragmented same-host http(s) URLs (same registrable host as the seed's final URL) and whose edges are <a href> links parsed from fetched HTML in document order. Non-http(s) schemes and asset extensions (png,jpg,jpeg,gif,svg,ico,css,js,pdf,zip,gz,woff,woff2,ttf,otf,mp4,webp,xml,rss,atom,epub,mobi,mp3,ogg,djvu,exe,iso) are excluded. JS-generated links are NOT edges (disclosed in validity note VN-V2).
operational_definitions.hop_distance: Graph shortest-path length in edges from the seed root (hop 0) to a page's URL, measured by the frozen policy. The seed URL itself is hop 0.
operational_definitions.state_carrying_item: A (page_url, control_name, control_type) tuple where the fetched page contains at least one named form control: an <input> with a non-empty name attribute or a <select> with a non-empty name attribute. The page is the observable; the item's hop is the page's hop.

bands.MID_excluded: hop == 2 (reported descriptively; excluded from the primary NEAR-vs-DEEP contrast to keep the bands separated)

operational_definitions.frozen_policy: Item-blind FIFO breadth-first crawl in document order from the seed root; per-site page budget B=250; depth cap D=6; each URL fetched at most once; the crawl stops as soon as the target page is fetched (for a per-item RED cost) or when budget/depth is exhausted (for the structural pass).
operational_definitions.primary_channel: GET requests (always valid on the stdlib substrate).
operational_definitions.size_channel: Sum of response-body bytes over the GETs charged to the arm. cl100k_base tokens are an OPTIONAL third channel: recorded only if `import tiktoken` succeeds and its version is recorded; otherwise the token fields are null and the byte channel is the declared size basis.

hypothesis: H1 (GROWING): on real sites, the unconditional item-blind re-derivation cost (RED) of a DEEP item (hop >= 3) is materially greater than that of a NEAR item (hop <= 1), by more than the materiality factor M=3.0, in both the request and size channels, because level-order frontier enumeration must fetch substantially more pages before a depth-h page is reached. If H1 holds, persistence of PATHS AND PROCEDURES has a positive, computable amortization surface and the break-even reuse count can be derived for the first time from a real re-derivation cost. H0 (FLAT): DEEP cost is within M=3.0x of NEAR cost in both channels because a detour-free shortest path reaches a deep item in about h GETs, making fresh-instance acquisition O(1) in site structure; then persistent cross-episode state cannot buy a work reduction that grows with Web depth and acquisition should be treated as a constant-cost deterministic procedure. The experiment does not presuppose which holds.

falsifier.statement: Let R_req = median(red.requests | DEEP) / median(red.requests | NEAR) and R_bytes = median(red.bytes | DEEP) / median(red.bytes | NEAR), with materiality factor M=3.0 pre-registered. FLAT branch (falsifies H1): R_req <= M AND R_bytes <= M. GROWING branch (supports H1): R_req > M AND R_bytes > M. Otherwise (channels disagree) the verdict is MIXED: report the per-channel direction and make NO O(1) claim. The ratio is undefined and the experiment is not scored if either band median is null or the admission gate fails; that is reported as MEASUREMENT_INVALID/status, never as a scientific branch.
falsifier.boundary_bracketed_by_live_values: M=3.0 lies strictly between the two live-measured calibration ratios (2.0 and 466.0), so the decision boundary is bracketed by observed instrument behaviour rather than assumed.

what_each_branch_means.FLAT: fresh-instance acquisition on this substrate class is O(1) in site structure; persistent state cannot buy a depth-growing work reduction; treat acquisition as constant-cost deterministic procedure and move effort to substrate expansion.
what_each_branch_means.GROWING: persistence of paths and procedures has a measurable amortization surface; compute the break-even reuse count from the real re-derivation cost.

measurement_validity.note: tiktoken is NOT importable in the DESIGN runner (ModuleNotFoundError confirmed). The primary cost basis is therefore GET requests (stdlib only) and the co-primary size basis is response-body bytes. cl100k_base tokens are recorded ONLY if EXECUTE can import tiktoken and records its version; otherwise token fields are null. No token figure may be presented as satisfying the frozen cost basis without a recorded tokenizer version. This repairs the parent's VN-11 (undeclared tokenizer).

Only static <a href> links are graph edges. JS-generated navigation (e.g., mdBook sidebars) is not followed, so measured hop is shortest-path over static same-host links and may be LONGER than a browser-observed hop. This is disclosed and applies identically to all bands.
Cross-host navigation is excluded, which can understate real Web depth; the claim is explicitly bounded to same-host static-link acquisition on this substrate class.

Given the frozen policy and a stable site, RED request count is deterministic; K=2 independent sessions per site are run to detect instability, and any site whose two sessions disagree on an item's hop or request count is flagged and excluded with a recorded reason.
If a seed host is unreachable at EXECUTE time, record status=BLOCKED and the exact error; never record network failure as a scientific branch. DESIGN confirmed all seed hosts reachable on 2026-10-09.
State-item discovery is an HTML-parser heuristic for named <input>/<select>; pages whose controls are JS-rendered are missed. Detection rate is reported per site.
hop==2 (MID) items are reported descriptively only and excluded from the primary NEAR-vs-DEEP contrast; the bands are disjoint by construction.
The candidate pool is dominated by the mdBook engine on doc.rust-lang.org; generalization is reported per-host and bounded, and is not claimed beyond the admitted hosts/engines.

break_even.paired_item_sets: Within each band, RED and both RACQ arms are measured over the SAME admitted item set, so every break-even ratio is a per-item quantity.

baseline_ordering_proof.claim: By construction RED >= RACQ_PATH >= RACQ_URL in both requests and bytes, with strict inequalities on any site that is not a detour-free chain.
argument: RACQ_URL issues exactly 1 GET (the item page) and bears that page's bytes.

RACQ_PATH issues exactly h+1 GETs (one per hop on the frozen shortest path). For h>=1, h+1 > 1, so RACQ_PATH.requests > RACQ_URL.requests; the path pages' bytes include the item page, so RACQ_PATH.bytes >= RACQ_URL.bytes.

RED is the item-blind BFS. Before fetching the item page at hop h, the BFS must fetch every page at levels 0..h-1 that it reaches and every level-h page that precedes the target in the frozen document order. The shortest-path pages are a subset of the pages RED fetches, so RED.requests >= RACQ_PATH.requests and RED.bytes >= RACQ_PATH.bytes.

RED.requests > RACQ_PATH.requests (strict) iff the BFS takes at least one detour GET before reaching the item page, i.e. iff the count of pages fetched at levels < h plus preceding level-h pages exceeds h. This occurs whenever some level < h has breadth > 1 or a preceding level-h page exists; it is the normal case on the admitted real sites and fails only on a detour-free linear chain.

Therefore the re-derivation comparator is strictly more expensive than persisted-path re-acquisition for every admitted item with >=1 detour, so the break-even denominator (RED.requests - RACQ_PATH.requests) is strictly positive and the accept region is non-empty. Detour-free items yield denominator 0 and are recorded as break-even-ineligible, which is the honest FLAT case rather than a fabricated saving.
baseline_ordering_proof.pre_freeze_arithmetic_witness: The live pre-freeze probe already observed the ordering on real data: POS_KNOWN_HOP_CONTROL target (hop 1, direct link) had RED.requests = 3 and cum_bytes = 653222, while RACQ_PATH.requests = 2 and RACQ_URL.requests = 1 -- RED > RACQ_PATH > RACQ_URL. The BROAD_FANOUT_CALIBRATION had RED.requests(hop3) = 932 versus RACQ_PATH.requests = 4, a strict >200x separation.
baseline_ordering_proof.parent_repair: This implements precondition (2), repairing the parent's empty accept region.

two_sided_reachability.why: Implements the Director's requirement that the falsifier be satisfiable in BOTH directions, and the discriminating-control prior that a certificate detecting only absence is uninterpretable.
two_sided_reachability.method: Two local stdlib http.server fixtures are run under the identical frozen policy and are reported as calibration controls, not as site results.
two_sided_reachability.boundary_bracketed: M=3.0 lies strictly between the two live-measured ratios, so both branches are demonstrably reachable by the frozen instrument.

decision_rule: Step 0: EXECUTE reproduces all four controls; any failure -> status=MEASUREMENT_INVALID, no branch. Step 1: run the structural pass on the candidate roots under the frozen policy; apply ADMISSION_GATE_V1; failure -> status=MEASUREMENT_INVALID with exact shortfall. Step 2: for each admitted item measure RED, RACQ_PATH, RACQ_URL in K=2 sessions. Step 3: compute per-site and pooled ratios with M=3.0. Verdict per site/pool: FLAT iff R_req<=3.0 AND R_bytes<=3.0; GROWING iff R_req>3.0 AND R_bytes>3.0; else MIXED. Step 4: report band medians and the break-even reuse counts for eligible items. The scientific outcome is GROWING (supports H1), FALSIFIES H1 (FLAT), or MIXED, written to result.json.outcome with status=COMPLETE. No outcome is recorded as a failure; only genuine measurement invalidity is status=MEASUREMENT_INVALID.
product_consequence_positive: If GROWING (H1 supported): persistence of PATHS AND PROCEDURES has a measurable amortization surface; the packet hands the first real depth-derived re-derivation cost and break-even reuse count to C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY, C-FRESHNESS staleness economics and the C-WEB-DYNAMICS timescales axis. A bounded successor may then implement a path/procedure cache in the product kernel with a measured break-even, subject to a separate verdict; this experiment does not promote any mechanism.
product_consequence_negative: If FLAT (H1 falsified): fresh-instance acquisition on this substrate class is O(1) in site structure; persistent cross-episode state cannot buy a work reduction that grows with Web depth. SPIDER should treat fresh-instance acquisition as a constant-cost deterministic procedure, stop optimizing acquisition on this substrate class, and move effort to substrate expansion and elsewhere. Path-persistence work is deprioritized with recorded evidence rather than by assertion.
estimated_cost: 6 candidate site roots; structural pass <= 250 GETs/site (<= 1500); cost pass K=2 sessions/site (<= 3000); RACQ_PATH/RACQ_URL charges are bounded by admitted-item counts and are small relative to RED; total <= ~5000 GETs, <= ~200 MB, wall-clock target <= 45 min. No browser, Docker, model key, credential, cookie or write verb. Agent-compute: 1 DESIGN + 1 EXECUTE + 1 AUDIT cycle.
expected_information_gain: High. The parent EXP-FRONTIER-37385647440 proved the cost question was never exercised at depth (every admitted item at hop <= 1). This experiment produces the first real re-derivation cost at hop >= 3 and a decision-changing FLAT-vs-GROWING answer: either acquisition is O(1) and path persistence is not an optimization target, or path/procedure persistence has a computable break-even. Both outcomes are decision-changing and neither needs a browser, Docker, credential, model key, write verb or unavailable asset.
